collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — TALL TALES AND SELF-INTEREST (TT-01 to TT-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Boasting, stretched stories, little vanities, wanting the credit, the best seat or the bigger half. Most of it is harmless and funny; kind people can be boastful too. Nobody is exposed for the sake of it, and nobody needs a lesson.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks two adults)

collection.description: A villager boasting of fearing nothing finds a large spider between their feet: stay very calm, or admit it.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has been explaining to (friend) that (subject.he/she) isn't afraid of anything: not storms, not the dark, not deep water, and certainly not spiders. At that exact moment, a large brown spider strolls out from under the woodpile and stops right between (subject)'s feet.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) stays very calm. So calm that (subject.he/she) doesn't move, doesn't blink, and makes a small, high noise through (subject.his/her) nose. (friend) gently scoops the spider onto a leaf and carries it off into the bushes. "I was letting it decide where to go," says (subject). "Of course you were," says (friend).

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) is on top of the woodpile before anyone sees (subject.him/her) move. "Except spiders," (subject.he/she) says from up there. "I forgot about spiders." (friend) laughs and carries the spider away. (subject) climbs down. "Storms, though. Not a bit afraid of storms." "I believe you," says (friend), and very nearly does.
